text:
“Um,” I say.

Mom scans the food as she blinks herself awake, and pulls out Halmoni’s plastic tub of kimchi. “Sound good?” she asks, holding it up.

I nod, not trusting myself to say anything. I glance over at the jar, but Mom’s too tired to notice.

She pushes herself up so she’s sitting on the counter and motions for me to join her.

I hesitate because this is not typical Mom behavior. But I hop up next to her, even though I’m partially waiting for her to scold me.

Mom just unscrews the lid and fishes out a piece of kimchi with her fingers. Then she drops the piece right into her mouth and smacks her lips.

When she holds the tub out to me, I stare at my mother. Any moment now, she’ll wake up and realize she was sleepwalking. And sleep-eating. And sleep-rule-breaking.

Mom laughs. “Lily. Stop looking at me like I have three heads.”

“It’s just . . .”

She pushes the kimchi tub closer. “Eat.”

So I take a piece of kimchi and chew it, letting the spicy-sour-salty flavor settle my stomach.

Maybe nothing is too weird in the middle of the night. Spirits might slip into these moments, between waking and dreaming—but love does, too.
